chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the charity of what has not been distributed and has not been seized (taken possession of). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible (to retract). The people intended the grant (Nuhlah), but they erred.'

key_terms.النُّحْل: The grant (a specific type of gift or provision)

ai.seo_question: Can charity be retracted before it is distributed and possessed?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that charity (*sadaqah*) remains revocable before full distribution and possession (*qabd*), correcting the popular misconception that it was irrevocable like *Nuhlah* (a specific grant). This ruling highlights the distinction between general charitable gifts and specific legal categories in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the default permissibility of retraction applies unless explicitly waived. The Imam’s explanation underscores the importance of understanding the specific legal definitions (*hukm*) versus common linguistic usage (*lughah*) in deriving fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Magra, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about charity what has not been distributed and not been seized (taken possession of). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It (retraction) is allowed. But rather, the people intended the grant, but they erred’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al-Mighra’ from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about charity which is not distributed or possessed by the recipient. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible (for the donor to use it); people had the intention to gift it but they made a mistake (in calling it a charity).”’
